diagnosis.summary: Product-service is experiencing severe DynamoDB read throttling, with 3,333 read throttle events per minute and p95 end-to-end latency at 3,195.7 ms against a baseline of 6.6 ms, a roughly 487x increase. The 5xx error rate on product-service stands at 2.81%, up from a baseline of 0. Payment-service request rate has also risen above its baseline at 2.03 rps versus 0.94 rps.
diagnosis.root_cause: DynamoDB read throttling on the Products table is the most likely root cause, with consumed read capacity and throttle counts far above baseline while write throttle events remain at zero.
evidence: product-service read_throttle_events rose from 0 to 3,333/min and throttled_requests rose from 0 to 2,181/min, both from a baseline of zero.
product-service db_consumed_read_capacity rose from 449.3 to 59,267.5 RCU/min, approximately 132x its baseline.
product-service db_latency_ms_p95 rose from 5.6 ms to 3,195.1 ms (roughly 569x baseline) and db_latency_ms_mean rose from 4.0 ms to 509.3 ms (roughly 126x baseline).
product-service p95_latency_ms rose from 6.6 ms to 3,195.7 ms, roughly 487x its baseline, and error_rate_5xx stands at 2.81% against a baseline of 0.
product-service write_throttle_events remain at 0, the same as baseline, indicating throttling is confined to reads.
payment-service request_rate is 2.03 rps against a baseline of 0.94 rps, roughly 2.15x its baseline.
recommended_actions: Raise the Products table provisioned read capacity or switch it to on-demand mode to relieve the read throttling immediately.
After changing capacity, recheck read_throttle_events and db_latency_ms_p95 to confirm the throttle counts and tail latency are returning toward baseline.

Reduce the read cost of GET /products by returning one page per call with a limit and next-page token instead of scanning the whole table, or cache the product list inside the Lambda function between invocations.
Keep SDK retry settings unchanged during the incident; reducing retry attempts would convert the current tail latency into a higher 5xx error rate.
Investigate the payment-service request rate increase in parallel, as it has risen to 2.03 rps from a baseline of 0.94 rps and may warrant separate attention.
